novel.justification: This is the paper's deliberate noninjective measurement regime. It covers applications with more latent mechanisms than observed coordinates and isolates the positive-real projection problem that injective recovery theorems do not address.

assumptions.condition: The labels in \(V\) form a topological order of \(G\).
\(\Lambda^{(0)}_{ij}\ne0\) if and only if \(j\to i\) is an edge of \(G\).
No two columns of \(F\) are collinear.

standard.name: Single-node soft intervention changing every incoming edge

novel.justification: This retained-edge soft-intervention condition describes perturbations that modify rather than delete active regulatory inputs; any continuously distributed perturbation away from the finitely many deletion values satisfies it almost surely.

assumptions.condition: The coordinates of \(\varepsilon^{(k)}\) are mutually independent in every context \(k\in K\).

definitions.name: \(\mathcal M_{p,q}(G)\)
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M_{p,q}(G)=\{(F,\Lambda^{(0)},\delta,v,t)\in\mathbb R^{pq+2q^2+2q}:2\le p<q,\ G\text{ is a DAG on }V\text{ in the displayed topological order},\operatorname{rank}(F)=p,\ F\text{ has nonzero pairwise-noncollinear columns},\Lambda^{(0)}_{ij}\ne0\Longleftrightarrow j\to i\text{ is an edge of }G,\operatorname{supp}(\delta_k)=\operatorname{pa}_G(k),\Lambda^{(0)}_{kj}+\delta_{kj}\ne0,\ v_i>0,\ t_i>0\}\). This positive-support semialgebraic ambient domain includes the variance-neutral hyperplanes \(t_i=v_i\). All equalities, strict inequalities, closures, relative interiors, and chambers below use the Euclidean relative topology of this ambient set or of a stated semialgebraic subset.

definitions.name: Finite theorem-specific exceptional-polynomial families
definitions.construction: For each theorem label \(s\), let \(\mathcal Q_s(p,G,G')\) be the finite list of graph-indexed polynomials explicitly named by that theorem. The family \(\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{term}}\) contains nonzero path minors and augmented affine-support minors. The family \(\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{branch}}\) contains nonzero rank minors, factor-line discriminants, denominator-cleared chart denominators, support residuals, and the theorem-specific variance-activity factor \(\prod_{k\in V}(t_k-v_k)\). For the fork pair, \(\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{fork}}\) adds every nonzero \(3\times3\) minor of \(B_{\ell}\), the displayed loading determinants, and maximal Jacobian minors of the denominator-cleared two-scalar systems. Each list is formed after deleting polynomials that vanish identically for the fixed graph pair. Variance neutrality is excluded only from covariance theorem loci, not from the ambient model or terminal theory.

definitions.name: Theorem-specific generic loci
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M^{\circ}_{s,p,q}(G,G')=\{\theta\in\mathcal M_{p,q}(G):\prod_{f\in\mathcal Q_s(p,G,G')}f(\theta)\ne0\}\) for \(s\in\{\mathrm{term},\mathrm{branch},\mathrm{fork},\mathrm{width}\}\), equipped with the relative Zariski topology inherited from the semialgebraic ambient domain. The factor \(\prod_{k\in V}(t_k-v_k)\) belongs only to the covariance families, so terminal compatibility is not restricted by variance activity.

definitions.name: Aligned population factorization input \(\mathcal R\)
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal R=[\{A^{(k)}\}_{k\in K},\{\mathcal L(\varepsilon^{(k)})\}_{k\in K}]_{\mathfrak M_q}\), where columns and independent non-Gaussian source laws are aligned across contexts. For \(M\in\mathfrak M_q\), the equivalence action is \(A^{(k)}\mapsto A^{(k)}M\) and \(\mathcal L(\varepsilon^{(k)})\mapsto\mathcal L(M^{-1}\varepsilon^{(k)})\) simultaneously for every \(k\in K\). Computation uses a rational projective gauge: after enumerating the common permutations compatible with the displayed topological order, scale each nonzero loading column so its least-index nonzero observed coordinate equals \(1\). Certificates are transported back over the simultaneous permutation orbit. This factorization datum is an explicit population input; its recovery from raw laws is not assumed inside the graph-compatibility map.

definitions.name: Factor-recovered actual-row support and closure
definitions.construction: Choose any representative of \(\mathcal R\). For each aligned target \(k\), solve the rank-one update \(A^{(k)}=A^{(0)}+a_kh_{\mathcal R,k}^{\mathsf T}\) with \(h_{\mathcal R,kk}=0\), and form \(H_{\mathcal R}\) from these rows. Define \(\mathcal C(\mathcal R)\) by \(i\to k\in\mathcal C(\mathcal R)\Longleftrightarrow(H_{\mathcal R})_{ki}\ne0\).

definitions.name: Observable-input graph classes
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal G_{\mathrm{soft}}(\mathcal R)=\{D:D\text{ is a DAG on }V,\ \overline D=\mathcal C(\mathcal R),\text{ and there exist }\theta\in\mathcal M_{p,q}(D)\text{ and independent centered non-Gaussian }\varepsilon^{(k)}\text{ with covariance }S^{(k)}\text{ whose aligned factorization represents }\mathcal R\}\). Also \(\mathcal G_{\mathrm{cov}}(\mathcal R,\{\Sigma^{(k)}\}_{k\in K})=\{D:D\text{ is a DAG on }V,\ \overline D=\mathcal C(\mathcal R),\text{ and some }\theta\in\mathcal M_{p,q}(D)\text{ generates every }\Sigma^{(k)}\}\). Both sets are taken modulo the common relabeling induced by \(\mathfrak M_q\).

definitions.name: Actual intervention-row matrix
definitions.construction: \(P=(I_q-\Lambda^{(0)})^{-1}\), \(h_k^{\mathsf T}=\delta_k^{\mathsf T}P\), and \(H=(h_1,\ldots,h_q)^{\mathsf T}\).

definitions.name: Terminal-copy graph \(G^{\mathrm{term}}\)
definitions.construction: Starting from \(G\), add a sink \(k^{\star}\) for each \(k\in V\); retain every baseline edge and add \(i\to k^{\star}\) with label \(\delta_{ki}\) for each \(i\in\operatorname{pa}_{G}(k)\).

definitions.name: Columnwise affine compatibility block
definitions.construction: For every \(j\in V\), set \(C_j=\operatorname{ch}_{G'}(j)\), \(R_j=\operatorname{de}_{G'}(j)\setminus C_j\), \(M_j=H[R_j,C_j]\), \(b_j=H[R_j,j]\), \(\mathcal A_j=\{x_j\in\mathbb R^{|C_j|}:M_jx_j=b_j\}\), and \(d_{ji}(x_j)=H[i,j]-H[i,C_j]x_j\) for \(i\in C_j\).

definitions.name: Definition 3.14 baseline-path class \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{obs}}(G)\)
definitions.construction: \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{obs}}(G)=\{G':\overline{G'}=\overline G,\ \operatorname{rank}P[R_j,C_j]=\operatorname{rank}P[R_j,C_j\cup\{j\}]\text{ for every }j\in V\text{ and every }\theta\in\mathcal M^{\circ}_{\mathrm{term},p,q}(G,G')\}\).

definitions.name: Corrected actual-row class \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{soft}}(G)\)
definitions.construction: \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{soft}}(G)=\{G':\overline{G'}=\overline G,\text{ for every }\theta\in\mathcal M^{\circ}_{\mathrm{term},p,q}(G,G')\text{ there exists }U=I_q-\Lambda'^{(0)}\text{ with exact support }G'\text{ such that }h_k^{\mathsf T}U\text{ has exact support }\operatorname{pa}_{G'}(k)\text{ and every candidate edge remains nonzero after its change for all }k\in V\}\).

definitions.name: Positive-real covariance twin set \(\mathcal E_p(G,G')\)
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal E_p(G,G')=\{\theta\in\mathcal M_{p,q}(G):\exists\theta'\in\mathcal M_{p,q}(G')\text{ with }\Sigma_{\theta'}^{(k)}=\Sigma_{\theta}^{(k)}\text{ for every }k\in K\}\). Candidate baseline and intervention variances are positive but may satisfy \(t'_k=v'_k\); variance activity is imposed only on a true theorem-specific generic locus.

definitions.name: Matched-existential covariance class \(\mathsf{soft2M}_{2,p}(G)\)
definitions.construction: \(\mathsf{soft2M}_{2,p}(G)=\{G':G'\text{ is a DAG on }V,\ \overline{G'}=\overline G,\ \mathcal E_p(G,G')\ne\varnothing\}\).

definitions.name: Generic positive-real covariance class \(\mathsf{Cov}_p(G)\)
definitions.construction: \(\mathsf{Cov}_p(G)=\{G':\overline{G'}=\overline G,\ C\setminus\operatorname{cl}_{C}(\mathcal E_p(G,G')\cap C)\text{ has empty }\operatorname{relint}_{C}\text{ for every full-dimensional connected semialgebraic chamber }C\text{ of }\mathcal M^{\circ}_{\mathrm{branch},p,q}(G,G')\}\), where the chambers fix the signs of the nonzero structural coefficients, changes, and \(t_k-v_k\), and closure and relative interior are taken in \(C\). This is a generic chamberwise functional and makes no pointwise assertion on the variance-neutral hyperplanes of the ambient model.

definitions.name: Worked fork covariance collision \(\mathcal W_{\mathrm{fork}}(T)\)
definitions.construction: For \(p=2\), \(q=4\), and \(T>0\), \(T\ne1\), set the true baseline loading and variances to \(A=\begin{psmallmatrix}1&2&7&4\\2&3&11&7\end{psmallmatrix}\) and \(v=(1,1,1,1)\); set \(\Lambda^{(0)}_{21}=\Lambda^{(0)}_{31}=\Lambda^{(0)}_{32}=\Lambda^{(0)}_{42}=1\), \(h_1=0\), \(h_2=(1,0,0,0)\), \(h_3=(3,1,0,0)\), \(h_4=(1,1,0,0)\), and \(t=(4,4,T,4)\), with \(F=A(I_4-\Lambda^{(0)})\). For the candidate set \(\Lambda'^{(0)}_{21}=4\), \(\Lambda'^{(0)}_{32}=\Lambda'^{(0)}_{42}=1\), \(F'=\begin{psmallmatrix}-7&-9&7&4\\-10&-15&11&7\end{psmallmatrix}\), \(v'=(1,1,1,1)\), \(h'_1=0\), \(h'_2=(1,0,0,0)\), \(h'_3=(32/11,8/11,0,0)\), \(h'_4=(-2,-1/2,0,0)\), and \(t'=(4,4,T+144/121,19/4)\). In both models define each change row by \(\delta_k^{\mathsf T}=h_k^{\mathsf T}(I_4-\Lambda^{(0)})\) and its primed analogue, and use independent centered non-Gaussian errors with the displayed variances.

definitions.name: Complete generic factor-line branch family \(\mathfrak B_p(G,G')\)
definitions.construction: For a same-transitive-closure pair of DAGs \(G,G'\) on \(V\) in their common topological order and \(\theta\in\mathcal M^{\circ}_{\mathrm{branch},p,q}(G,G')\), fix one common-permutation representative, factor each \(D_k\) as \(D_k=\ell_km_k^{\mathsf T}+m_k\ell_k^{\mathsf T}\), choose one of its two real factor lines for each nonroot and its unique line for each root, and put every chosen line in the rational projective gauge whose least-index nonzero observed coordinate is \(1\). For that choice impose \(L\operatorname{diag}(v')L^{\mathsf T}=\Sigma^{(0)}\), \(Lz_k+\rho_k\ell_k=m_k\), \(z_k\) supported on \(\operatorname{an}_{G'}(k)\), \(t'_k=v'_k+2\rho_k-\sum_i z_{ki}^2/v'_i>0\), \(\delta_k'{}^{\mathsf T}=z_k^{\mathsf T}\operatorname{diag}(v')^{-1}U\), and every exact-support, retained-edge, and mixing-column inequation; \(\mathfrak B_p(G,G')\) is the resulting family of at most \(2^{q-r}\) systems for that representative. Candidate variance-neutral branches remain legal.

definitions.name: Eight explicit bivariate fork systems
definitions.construction:
For each of the eight loading-line choices, form \(B_{\ell}=[(\ell_{k1}^2,\ell_{k1}\ell_{k2},\ell_{k2}^2)^{\mathsf T}]_{k=1}^{4}\), solve \(v'=v'_0+sn\) with \(n\in\ker B_{\ell}\setminus\{0\}\), write \(m_2=\zeta\ell_1+ho_2\ell_2\), and set \(g=v'_1x\ell_1+v'_2\ell_2\). For \(k\in\{3,4\}\), impose \( eta_k=\det[m_k,\ell_k]/\det[g,\ell_k]\), \(m_k- eta_kg=ho_k\ell_k\), \(h'_2=(\zeta/v'_1,0,0,0)\), \(h'_k= eta_k(x,1,0,0)\), \(t'_2=v'_2+2ho_2-\zeta^2/v'_1\), and \(t'_k=v'_k+2ho_k- eta_k^2(v'_1x^2+v'_2)\). The system includes \(v'_i>0\), \(t'_i>0\), \(x
e0\), \(x+\zeta/v'_1
e0\), \(\zeta eta_3 eta_4\det[g,\ell_3]\det[g,\ell_4]
e0\), the stated mixing noncollinearities, and finite hyperplane avoidance for the remaining coefficients \(\Lambda'^{(0)}_{32}\) and \(\Lambda'^{(0)}_{42}\). Candidate equalities \(t'_i=v'_i\) are not excluded. Thus each legal branch is a rational sign system only in \(s\) and \(x\).

definitions.name: Graph and sparse-polynomial bit model
definitions.construction: Encode \(p\) and \(q\) in binary, encode \(G\) and \(G'\) by their \(q\times q\) adjacency bit matrices in the common topological order, and encode every denominator-cleared input branch polynomial sparsely by binary exponent vectors and signed binary integer coefficients. The encoding lists every chart denominator, denominator-clearing inequation, variance-positivity polynomial, covariance-cone minor, exact-support and retained-edge residual, mixing nonzero and noncollinearity factor, and theorem-specific exceptional factor, together with sparse degree and coefficient height. Let \(B=|\operatorname{Enc}(p,G,G')|_{\mathrm{bit}}\) be this pre-solution input length; certificate coefficient growth is part of the output complexity to be bounded.

definitions.name: Positive-real frontier compiler handle \(\mathfrak C_p(G,G')\)
definitions.construction: Build the target compiler from terminal-copy min-cut certificates, the sparse factor-line systems \(\mathfrak B_p(G,G')\), common-topological elimination, running \(p(p+1)/2\)-moment accumulators, recursive faces of the baseline covariance cone, Schur-complement sign cells, and branch-gluing certificates. For bounded \(\omega_p(G,G')\), use local subresultant and Thom-sign tables on the elimination bags. In each chamber, the output is either a relatively dense positive-real realization cover or a full-dimensional linkage, affine, covariance-cone-face, or positivity separator in the bit model \(\operatorname{Enc}(p,G,G')\).

definitions.name: Covariance-terminal elimination width \(\omega_p(G,G')\)
definitions.construction: For a common topological elimination order, expose the denominator-cleared factor-line constraints node by node; retain a latent node while it occurs in an unprocessed ancestor-support equation or terminal-copy linkage, and summarize processed baseline covariance terms by a running vector in \(\mathbb R^{p(p+1)/2}\). The active frontier is the retained latent set together with this fixed moment state. Define \(\omega_p(G,G')\) as the minimum, over common topological elimination orders and legal terminal-copy decompositions, of the largest active-frontier cardinality. A pair is \(w\)-tractable when \(\omega_p(G,G')\le w\).

statements.statement: For every \(G'\) with \(\overline{G'}=\overline G\) and every \(\theta\in\mathcal M^{\circ}_{\mathrm{term},p,q}(G,G')\), \(G'\in\mathsf H_{\mathrm{soft}}(G)\) if and only if, for every \(j\in V\), the affine space \(\mathcal A_j\) is nonempty and none of \(x_{ji}\), \(d_{ji}(x_j)\), or \(x_{ji}+d_{ji}(x_j)\), for \(i\in C_j\), vanishes identically on \(\mathcal A_j\). For all \(R,C\subseteq V\), \(\operatorname{rank}H[R,C]\) equals the maximum number of vertex-disjoint paths from \(C\) to terminal copies \(R^{\star}\) in \(G^{\mathrm{term}}\). These conditions give sound and complete membership and nonmembership certificates in \(O(q^5)\) rational-function field operations. The baseline-path class in Definition 3.14 agrees with corrected actual-row compatibility exactly when these tests agree with its baseline inverse-path rank tests for every same-closure candidate \(G'\); this is an exact finite graph-input decision procedure, and the four-node counterexample below proves that the equivalence asserted by Theorem 3.15 is false without this agreement condition. This structural result holds throughout the positive-variance ambient model, including \(t_k=v_k\).
statements.justification: This is the corrected sound-and-complete combinatorial answer to the compatibility problem before covariance projection.
statements.gap: Equation (20) of Leyes Carreno et al. correctly derives compatibility from the actual rows \(\Delta^{(k)}_{k,\cdot}\), but the proof of Theorem 3.15 replaces their independent changes by baseline coefficients to reach Definition 3.14. Terminal-copy linkage and affine nonvanishing repair precisely that rank step and add exact-support and retained-edge certificates.
statements.consumer: This gives the corrected compatible DAG set and auditable linkage or affine certificates requested by Problem 5.1.

statements.statement: Theorem 3.15 of Leyes Carreno, Meroni, and Seigal is false as written. Let \(G_{\times}=\{1\to2,2\to3,3\to4,1\to3\}\), let \(G_{\mathrm{ch}}=\{1\to2,2\to3,3\to4\}\), and consider \(j=1\), so \(C_1=\{2\}\) and \(R_1=\{3,4\}\). With \(\alpha=\Lambda^{(0)}_{21}\), \(b=\Lambda^{(0)}_{32}\), \(d=\Lambda^{(0)}_{31}\), \(\beta=\delta_{32}\), \(\delta=\delta_{31}\), and \(\gamma=\delta_{43}\), the two actual-row rank matrices derived from Equation (20) are \[M_{G_{\times},G_{\mathrm{ch}}}[1]=H[\{3,4\},\{2\}]=\begin{pmatrix}\beta\\ \gamma b\end{pmatrix},\qquad \bigl(M_{G_{\times},G_{\mathrm{ch}}}[1]\mid b_{G_{\times},G_{\mathrm{ch}}}[1]\bigr)=H[\{3,4\},\{2,1\}]=\begin{pmatrix}\beta&\delta+\alpha\beta\\ \gamma b&\gamma(d+\alpha b)\end{pmatrix}.\] The augmented determinant is \(\gamma(\beta d-b\delta)\). It is not the zero polynomial: \(\alpha=b=c=d=\beta=\gamma=1\), \(\delta=2\), and \(\delta_{21}=1\) give value \(-1\), while every true edge and every intervention change is nonzero and each changed coefficient is retained. Hence it is nonzero on a relative Zariski-open subset allowed by Assumption 1.2 and the exact-support and retained-edge conditions, where the two ranks are \(1\) and \(2\). The specialization \((\beta,\delta)=(b,d)\) used in the proof of Theorem 3.15 identifies independent parameter variables and changes the determinant to \(\gamma(bd-bd)=0\), dropping the augmented rank to \(1\). Thus \(G_{\mathrm{ch}}\in\mathsf H_{\mathrm{obs}}(G_{\times})\) but \(G_{\mathrm{ch}}\notin\mathsf H_{\mathrm{soft}}(G_{\times})\) on \(\mathcal M^{\circ}_{\mathrm{term},p,4}(G_{\times},G_{\mathrm{ch}})\), throughout the positive-variance ambient domain.
statements.justification: The explicit indexed matrices isolate the invalid generic-rank substitution and prove that the corrected graph class differs on an admissible open set.
statements.gap: The proof of Theorem 3.15 first uses the correct actual \(\Delta^{(k)}\) rows, then replaces each independent change \(\lambda^{(k)}_{ki}-\lambda^{(0)}_{ki}\) by \(\lambda^{(0)}_{ki}\) while claiming generic rank is preserved; the displayed minor proves that this nongeneric specialization can lower rank.
statements.consumer: This is a Problem 5.1 regression test preventing the LCD workflow from certifying a chain that violates the actual changed mechanism rows.

statements.statement: For every \(\theta\in\mathcal M_{p,q}(G)\), \((I_q-\Lambda^{(k)})^{-1}=P+Pe_kh_k^{\mathsf T}\), \(\Delta^{(k)}=Pe_kh_k^{\mathsf T}\), \(\Delta^{(k)}_{k,\cdot}=h_k^{\mathsf T}\), \(A^{(k)}=A+a_kh_k^{\mathsf T}\), and \[D_k=a_k(ASh_k)^{\mathsf T}+(ASh_k)a_k^{\mathsf T}+(h_k^{\mathsf T}Sh_k+t_k-v_k)a_ka_k^{\mathsf T}.\] For every same-transitive-closure pair of DAGs \(G,G'\) on \(V\) in their common topological order and every \(\theta\in\mathcal M^{\circ}_{\mathrm{branch},p,q}(G,G')\), the systems in \(\mathfrak B_p(G,G')\) represent every legal positive-real covariance twin and no illegal twin, including candidate variance-neutral twins, every factor-line choice in the fixed rational projective gauge, all common latent permutations, support inequations, and all semialgebraic sign and variance chambers relative to \(\mathcal M_{p,q}(G)\). Exact structural-row change makes the two rank-one directions generically nonproportional at each non-source; at a source, \(h_k=0\), so \(t_k=v_k\) makes the entire intervention null. The factor \(\prod_{k\in V}(t_k-v_k)\) excludes only that nongeneric source-null locus, together with variance-neutral non-source hyperplanes, from the covariance statement. The exceptional product is nonzero on every full-dimensional ambient chamber, and both signs of each true variance change are covered; no pointwise assertion is made on the excluded hyperplanes.
statements.justification: This lemma is the lossless bridge from observed covariance differences to a finite collection of positive candidate mechanisms.
statements.gap: Leyes Carreno et al. give a special overcomplete perfect-intervention covariance nonidentifiability example, not a complete soft-intervention factor-line reduction with positivity.
statements.consumer: This is the exhaustive algebraic input for the robust covariance refinement motivated by Problem 5.2 and for the companion LCD workflow's covariance-alternative report.

statements.statement:
For every \(T>0\), \(T
e1\), the two rational parameter points in \(\mathcal W_{\mathrm{fork}}(T)\) lie in the semialgebraic ambient domains for \(G_{\mathrm{fork}}\) and \(G'_{\mathrm{fork}}\), satisfy the required independent centered non-Gaussian distribution conditions, and obey \(\Sigma^{(k)}_{\mathrm{true}}=\Sigma^{(k)}_{\mathrm{candidate}}\) for all five contexts \(k\in K\). The candidate variances \(T+144/121\) and \(19/4\) are positive, all mixing columns are pairwise noncollinear, every changed edge is nonzero and retained, and the corresponding actual-row compatibility obstruction equals \(-2\), so \(G'_{\mathrm{fork}}
otin\mathsf H_{\mathrm{soft}}(G_{\mathrm{fork}})\). No algebraic-independence convention is imposed; membership in a theorem-specific generic locus is determined only by its finite exceptional-polynomial list. The displayed family lies off every true variance-neutral hyperplane because \(T
e1\); the collision and actual-row obstruction do not rely on excluding candidate variance-neutral models.
statements.justification: The explicit rational branch demonstrates that strict positivity is substantive and supplies a checkable worked instance for the compiler.
statements.gap: The anchor contains no positive overcomplete soft-intervention collision with all contexts, support constraints, and actual-row separation checked simultaneously.
statements.consumer: The five covariance identities and the \(-2\) obstruction are a regression fixture for the robust positive-real branch analysis motivated by Problem 5.2.

statements.statement: For \(p=2\) and \((G_{\mathrm{fork}},G'_{\mathrm{fork}})\), the eight loading-line choices are sound and complete on \(\mathcal M^{\circ}_{\mathrm{fork},2,4}(G_{\mathrm{fork}},G'_{\mathrm{fork}})\), and the finite product defining this locus, including \(\prod_{k\in V}(t_k-v_k)\), is nonzero on every full-dimensional ambient chamber. On each branch, \(v'=v'_0+sn\), \(m_2=\zeta\ell_1+\rho_2\ell_2\), and \(g=v'_1x\ell_1+v'_2\ell_2\); for \(k\in\{3,4\}\), \(\beta_k=\det[m_k,\ell_k]/\det[g,\ell_k]\), \(m_k-\beta_kg=\rho_k\ell_k\), \(h'_k=\beta_k(x,1,0,0)\), and \(t'_k=v'_k+2\rho_k-\beta_k^2(v'_1x^2+v'_2)\), while \(h'_2=(\zeta/v'_1,0,0,0)\) and \(t'_2=v'_2+2\rho_2-\zeta^2/v'_1\). A finite bivariate sign decomposition in \((s,x)\), together with the exact support hyperplane exclusions, classifies the union over every full-dimensional true sign and variance chamber \(C\subset\mathcal M^{\circ}_{\mathrm{fork},2,4}(G_{\mathrm{fork}},G'_{\mathrm{fork}})\) and returns either a legal-twin cover dense relative to \(C\) or a separator with full dimension relative to \(C\), verified in the original five covariance equations. Legal twins may be variance-neutral. In addition, for each \(T>0\), \(T\ne1\), there is a relatively open semialgebraic neighborhood of \(\mathcal W_{\mathrm{fork}}(T)\) inside its generic chamber and a legal covariance-twin branch on that neighborhood, certified by a nonzero Jacobian minor from \(\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{fork}}\). Both signs of every true variance change are covered; no pointwise assertion is made on a true variance-neutral hyperplane.
statements.justification: This is the mandatory first proved deliverable and the early kill test for whether graph-specific branch geometry can replace unrestricted real quantifier elimination.
statements.gap: The closest LCD results give neither an exhaustive positive eight-branch classification nor a nonsingular open covariance collision checked against every original context equation.
statements.consumer: This supplies the smallest auditable instance of the positive-real classification motivated by Problem 5.2 and the template the general compiler must reproduce.

statements.statement: For every \(2\le p<q\) and every DAG \(G\), \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{soft}}(G)\subseteq\mathsf{Cov}_p(G)\) for the generic chamberwise covariance functional. The claim covers both signs of every true variance change, makes no pointwise assertion on \(t_k=v_k\), and allows candidate twins with \(t'_k=v'_k\).
statements.justification: The nesting gives the information-order direction needed before equality or strict covariance surplus can be meaningful.
statements.gap: Problem 5.2 motivates an information comparison for the published classes. Corrected actual-row compatibility and the chamberwise robust covariance class change both objects, so their nesting requires a separate result and is not an asserted identification with the published covariance-compatible class.
statements.consumer: This fixes the information-order direction needed to interpret robust covariance-only alternatives in the companion LCD workflow.

statements.statement: The recovered relation satisfies \(\mathcal C(\mathcal R)=\overline G\) up to the common latent permutation on \(\mathcal M^{\circ}_{\mathrm{term},p,q}(G,G)\cap\mathcal M^{\circ}_{\mathrm{branch},p,q}(G,G)\). The maps \(\mathcal R\mapsto\mathcal G_{\mathrm{soft}}(\mathcal R)\) and \((\mathcal R,\{\Sigma^{(k)}\}_{k\in K})\mapsto\mathcal G_{\mathrm{cov}}(\mathcal R,\{\Sigma^{(k)}\}_{k\in K})\) are invariant to the choice of representative of \(\mathcal R\) under \(\mathfrak M_q\). The rational projective gauge fixes every nonzero diagonal scale, and enumeration over the common permutation orbit leaves terminal ranks, exact-support inequations, covariance branches, realization covers, and separators invariant. If the inputs arise from \(\theta\in\mathcal M^{\circ}_{\mathrm{term},p,q}(G,G)\cap\mathcal M^{\circ}_{\mathrm{branch},p,q}(G,G)\cap\mathcal M^{\circ}_{s,p,q}(G,G')\) for the relevant covariance theorem label \(s\), then \(\mathcal G_{\mathrm{soft}}(\mathcal R)=\{\Pi_M(G'):G'\in\mathsf H_{\mathrm{soft}}(G),\ M\in\mathfrak M_q\}\) and \(\mathcal G_{\mathrm{cov}}(\mathcal R,\{\Sigma^{(k)}\}_{k\in K})=\{\Pi_M(G'):G'\in\mathsf{Cov}_{p}(G),\ M\in\mathfrak M_q\}\), where \(\Pi_M\) is the permutation part of \(M\). Hence the target is a functional of the explicit aligned factor input and covariance tuple, not a functional indexed by an unobserved true graph. This generic observable statement makes no pointwise assertion when a true variance change vanishes.
statements.justification: This proposition makes the population target invariant to the unavoidable latent permutation and scaling ambiguity.
statements.gap: The comparator results recover latent factors or graph classes only up to relabeling; they do not state this corrected covariance-versus-actual-row pair as one quotient-valued data functional.
statements.consumer: This supplies the companion LCD workflow with a quotient-valued graph-class target for the Problem 5.1 correction and the robust covariance refinement motivated by Problem 5.2.

statements.statement: Fix \(w\ge0\). For every \(2\le p<q\) and same-transitive-closure pair of DAGs \((G,G')\) on \(V\), written in their common topological order, with \(\omega_p(G,G')\le w\), the compiler \(\mathfrak C_p(G,G')\) is sound and complete for deciding \(G'\in\mathsf{Cov}_p(G)\setminus\mathsf H_{\mathrm{soft}}(G)\) on every full-dimensional chamber of \(\mathcal M^{\circ}_{\mathrm{branch},p,q}(G,G')\). Its acceptance certificate is a finite tree of rational univariate representations and Thom signs whose projected cells form a relatively dense positive-real realization cover; its rejection certificate is a terminal-linkage, affine-support, covariance-cone-face, or strict-positivity separator with bagwise subresultant verification. If \(B=|\operatorname{Enc}(p,G,G')|_{\mathrm{bit}}\), the algorithm uses at most \(\widetilde O\!\left(q(B+q+1)^{2^{w+3}}\right)\) bit operations and every certificate coefficient has bit length at most \((B+q+1)^{2^{w+2}}\). The proof uses only local sign determination on width-\(w\) bags and branch gluing. If the undirected union of \(G\) and \(G'\) has pathwidth at most \(w\) and both DAGs have maximum indegree at most \(w\), then \(\omega_p(G,G')\le p(p+1)/2+(w+1)(w+2)\); hence bounded-pathwidth, bounded-indegree pairs, including directed chains and bounded-width polytrees, form an explicit infinite tractable family. The theorem-specific locus excludes \(\prod_{k\in V}(t_k-v_k)=0\), covers both adjacent sign chambers, admits variance-neutral candidate twins, and makes no pointwise claim on excluded true hyperplanes.
statements.justification: This theorem supplies the required tractable family and converts the fork's local sign analysis into a graph-controlled exact compiler before any all-graph claim.
statements.gap: Foygel Barber et al. study half-trek criteria for identifiability of latent-variable models, while Sections IV--V of Kela et al. provide semidefinite tests and positive-semidefinite decomposition and realization machinery for latent causal structures. Wu et al. accelerate general existential Fourier--Motzkin elimination and cylindrical algebraic decomposition by tree dynamic programming over the primal graph of variables co-occurring in atomic constraints. Covariance-terminal width instead counts a domain-specific active latent frontier and one \(p(p+1)/2\)-dimensional moment state; neither width is known to dominate the other without a quantitative translation theorem. The output distinction is a dense positive-real realization cover or full-dimensional graph-frontier separator, not a claimed improvement over the complexity frontier of general quantifier elimination.
statements.consumer: For bounded-width gene-regulatory and measurement graphs, the LCD workflow obtains a terminating exact certificate instead of an unrestricted semialgebraic oracle.

statements.statement: Extend the bounded-width compiler to every \(2\le p<q\) and every same-transitive-closure pair \((G,G')\). Decide whether \(G'\in\mathsf{Cov}_p(G)\setminus\mathsf H_{\mathrm{soft}}(G)\) over every legal positive-real factor-line branch in each full-dimensional sign and variance chamber \(C\subset\mathcal M^{\circ}_{\mathrm{branch},p,q}(G,G')\). Prove soundness, completeness, and termination without unrestricted real quantifier elimination. On acceptance return a finite chamberwise dense positive-real realization cover; on rejection return a checkable full-dimensional linkage, affine, covariance-cone-face, or positivity separator. Give a closed-form bit-operation and coefficient-growth bound in \(p\), \(q\), \(B\), and the realized branch-interaction structure, and derive infinite equality and generic-strictness families. The theorem-specific locus may exclude \(\prod_{k\in V}(t_k-v_k)=0\); candidate twins may be variance-neutral, both signs of each true variance change must be covered, and no pointwise claim is made on the excluded hyperplanes.
statements.justification: This is the unresolved theorem-level frontier: a graph-specific positive-real decision principle for all noninjective soft-LCD systems.
statements.gap: Problem 5.2 motivates covariance-versus-higher-cumulant strictness for the published source model. The class \(\mathsf{Cov}_p(G)\) is instead a robust generic-chamber refinement internal to \(\mathcal M_{p,q}\); convex, birational, and half-trek results do not yield its all-graph projection completeness.
statements.consumer: The companion LCD workflow can use acceptance certificates to report genuine covariance alternatives and rejection certificates to justify when higher cumulants remove them.

sampling_model.design: Population identification from one baseline and one unknown-target single-node soft-intervention context per latent node under noninjective mixing \(2\le p<q\).
sampling_model.units: Inputs are aligned population factorization data \(\mathcal R\) and the \(q+1\) population covariance matrices \(\{\Sigma^{(k)}\}_{k\in K}\); there is no finite-sample claim.
sampling_model.treatment: Each non-source context changes every incoming coefficient of one unknown latent target and retains every such edge. Targets are identified only up to one common latent permutation.
sampling_model.overlap: No treatment-overlap condition applies. Baseline and intervention variances are positive and may coincide. Covariance theorems use only declared finite generic loci, including \(\prod_{k\in V}(t_k-v_k)\ne0\), cover both adjacent sign chambers, and make no pointwise claim on neutral hyperplanes.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Aligned factor directions and source laws modulo common permutation and diagonal scaling are population inputs. Recovery from raw laws and finite-sample tensor estimation are outside scope.

tldr: For noninjective soft-intervention linear causal disentanglement, \(2\le p<q\), covariance compatibility is a finite union of positive-real factor-line projections rather than an injective recovery problem. The information-frontier headline is a graph-specific compiler deciding whether a same-closure candidate lies generically in \(\mathsf{Cov}_p(G)\setminus\mathsf H_{\mathrm{soft}}(G)\), returning a positive realization cover or full-dimensional separator without unrestricted real quantifier elimination. This robust generic-chamber refinement is motivated by Problem 5.2, lies definitionally inside the matched-existential class \(\mathsf{soft2M}_{2,p}(G)\), and is not identified with the published covariance-compatible class. The mandatory first result completely classifies all eight branches of a \(p=2,q=4\) fork; the next proves the compiler on bounded covariance-terminal width with an explicit bit bound. Independently, compatibility is certified from the actual rows \(h_k^{\mathsf T}=\delta_k^{\mathsf T}(I_q-\Lambda^{(0)})^{-1}\) by terminal-copy linkage and affine support tests, and an explicit four-node minor refutes the generic-rank substitution in Theorem 3.15. Variance-neutral points remain in the ambient model: \(\prod_k(t_k-v_k)\ne0\) occurs only in theorem-specific covariance loci, and excluded hyperplanes receive no pointwise claim.

project_justification.gap: Problem 5.2 of Leyes Carreno, Meroni, and Seigal asks whether its covariance-compatible and higher-cumulant-compatible graph classes differ, but its overcomplete example proves parameter nonuniqueness rather than a graph-specific positive-real frontier. The robust class \(\mathsf{Cov}_p(G)\) refines the genericity requirement chamber by chamber, is definitionally contained in \(\mathsf{soft2M}_{2,p}(G)\), and is not identified with the published covariance-compatible class. Existing positive-semidefinite compatibility, affine-birational constraint transfer, half-trek criteria, equivalence-class recovery from unpaired interventions, and treewidth-accelerated general quantifier elimination do not decide the coupled noninjective branch union with the required realization-or-separator output. In the same paper, Equation (20) correctly derives compatibility from actual intervention rows, but the proof of Theorem 3.15 reaches the baseline-path class in Definition 3.14 by a nongeneric identification of independent change and baseline variables.
project_justification.niche: When \(p<q\), each rank-two covariance difference supplies two possible loading lines, while all contexts share one positive baseline decomposition and one candidate structural inverse. This finite nonconvex union must be decided chamber by chamber. Covariance-terminal width gives a graph-controlled route between one solved fork and the unrestricted problem.
project_justification.fill: The paper first proves the complete eight-branch \(p=2,q=4\) classification, then a realization-or-separator compiler for bounded covariance-terminal width with explicit certificate and bit complexity, and finally poses the all-graph compiler as the sole open information-frontier question. A separate terminal-copy theorem gives the corrected actual-row compatibility test, and a four-node counterexample identifies the precise invalid specialization in Theorem 3.15.

Theorem 1.7 uses Theorem 3.15 to state recovery of that soft-compatible class, and Problems 5.1--5.2 ask for a combinatorial description and whether covariance enlarges the compatible DAG set. technical_internal_limitation: Exact symbolic evidence establishes the actual-row determinant obstruction, a lossless regular reduction of the \(p=2,q=4\) fork to eight bivariate systems, and a rational covariance collision with positive candidate variances \(T+144/121\) and \(19/4\) for every \(T>0\), \(T\ne1\). These checks do not complete the eight-branch chamber classification. The width definition and local sign-decomposition bound must be proved to compose under branch gluing. Only covariance generic loci contain \(\prod_{k\in V}(t_k-v_k)\), so no pointwise variance-neutral conclusion is claimed.
honest_scope: Every information-frontier statement is restricted to noninjective mixing \(2\le p<q\); no novelty or equality claim is made for \(p=q\). All graph pairs are DAGs on the same node set, have common transitive closure, and are written in a common topological order. The ambient model includes all \(v_k>0\) and \(t_k>0\), including \(t_k=v_k\). Only theorem-specific covariance loci exclude \(\prod_{k\in V}(t_k-v_k)=0\); both adjacent signs are covered, candidate twins may be variance-neutral, and excluded true hyperplanes receive no pointwise claim. The definitional relation \(\mathsf{Cov}_p(G)\subseteq\mathsf{soft2M}_{2,p}(G)\) is non-headline. Containment in, equality with, or strict inclusion relative to the published covariance-compatible class is outside the claims until every maintained positive-real exact-support witness is checked against the source model. Common permutations are enumerated, nonzero diagonal scales are fixed by the rational projective gauge, and the quotient proposition certifies invariance of all outputs. The mandatory first proof is the full eight-branch fork classification against the original five covariance equations. The bounded-width compiler, including its certificate and bit bound, is next; the all-graph compiler is explicitly open. Terminal-copy compatibility is an independent structural correction. As a sanity reduction, when a branch has a unique positive baseline decomposition and every nonroot loading difference has only one graph-admissible line, the branch system reduces to the terminal affine tests and returns no covariance-only alternative. Recovery of aligned factors from raw laws, finite-sample inference, multitarget interventions, and nonlinear mixing are outside scope.

novelty_justification: Problem 5.2 and Proposition 3.6 of Leyes Carreno, Meroni, and Seigal (2025) motivate the destination: they do not classify which distinct DAGs survive every legal positive-real covariance branch under noninjective soft interventions. The class \(\mathsf{Cov}_p(G)\) is a robust generic-chamber refinement, is definitionally contained in \(\mathsf{soft2M}_{2,p}(G)\), and is not identified with the published covariance-compatible class. Zhang, Greenewald, Squires et al. recover an equivalence class from unpaired observational and interventional data under generalized faithfulness, but neither give nor rule out this noninjective positive-real covariance frontier. The closest methods also include the semidefinite and positive-semidefinite realization machinery of Kela et al., the affine-birational constraint-transfer results of Boege and Solus, the half-trek criteria of Foygel Barber et al., and the primal-treewidth quantifier-elimination framework of Wu et al. None supplies a finite non-birational branch union coupled through one mixing matrix and one structural inverse with a dense positive-real realization cover or full-dimensional separator. No complexity domination over Wu et al. is claimed. The strict deliverable is staged: a complete \(p=2,q=4\) eight-branch classification, then a bounded covariance-terminal-width compiler with explicit certificates and bit complexity, followed by the all-graph open question. Independently, the terminal theorem preserves the actual rows already derived in Equation (20), replaces the invalid change-to-baseline specialization in Theorem 3.15 by terminal-copy linkage, and adds exact-support and retained-edge affine screens. No novelty claim is made for \(p=q\).
